metadata.description: Sub-vertical seasonal hiring overrides for the activation event calendar (gold_standard.build_activation_calendar). Generic industry-level seasonality (e.g. 'Logistics & Supply Chain' = e-commerce/freight, peak Aug-Nov) is wrong for narrower sub-verticals whose real-world demand driver differs (e.g. propane/heating-fuel delivery peaks in winter). When a plan's client name / industry / role titles / notes match a sub-vertical's keywords, its monthly_profile REPLACES the generic month-by-month calendar entries (season/hiring_intensity/events/recommendation) for that plan. General, extensible mechanism -- add new sub-verticals here as they are identified (e.g. tax season for accounting, summer peak for landscaping); do not hardcode new sub-verticals into gold_standard.py itself.
metadata.hiring_intensity_scale: very_high | high | moderate | low -- same scale build_activation_calendar already uses for the generic calendar, so overridden months blend into the same budget_weight formula.

fuel_heating_delivery.label: Fuel & Heating Delivery
fuel_heating_delivery.rationale: Propane/heating-fuel delivery demand is driven by winter heating season (roughly Nov-Mar in most US climates), the inverse of generic freight/e-commerce logistics seasonality (which peaks Aug-Nov for holiday shipping volume). Hiring must ramp in the preceding Aug-Oct window so delivery drivers are trained, licensed, and route-assigned BEFORE the Oct-Mar heating peak -- not wound down heading into winter the way a generic logistics calendar would suggest. DOT compliance deadlines and CDL-school graduation cycles are climate-independent and are retained from the generic trucking calendar.
fuel_heating_delivery.source: Domain reasoning, not a fabricated statistic: propane/heating-fuel delivery volume tracks heating-degree-days (NOAA), which are highest Nov-Mar across most of the US; this profile expresses that as hiring-intensity weights and staffing rationale, the same way the generic calendar does, rather than inventing a numeric benchmark.

events: Peak propane demand -- crews already staffed, backfill only
1.recommendation: Peak delivery season is underway with crews already staffed; budget shifts to retention/backfill, not net-new ramp.

2.recommendation: Maintain backfill-only hiring through the remainder of heating season.

3.recommendation: Demand is tapering -- shift to passive sourcing and pipeline-building for next season.

4.recommendation: Lowest-demand window of the year -- minimal active recruiting spend.

5.recommendation: Hold spend low; use the quiet season for employer-branding content.

6.recommendation: Continue minimal spend -- last full month before the pre-season ramp must begin.

events: CDL school Q2 grads enter market
7.recommendation: Begin ramping recruiting spend -- drivers hired now have time to complete training and licensing before peak season.

8.recommendation: Increase spend significantly -- crews must be fully staffed and trained before the Oct-Mar heating peak.

events: CDL school Q3 grads enter market
9.recommendation: Maximum recruiting spend -- this is the critical staffing window ahead of winter demand.

10.recommendation: Close remaining staffing gaps now; last efficient hiring window before demand peaks.

11.recommendation: Shift from acquisition to retention -- crews should already be in place as heating demand ramps.

12.recommendation: Full staffing should already be in effect; budget toward retention and overtime coverage, not new-hire acquisition.

senior_living.label: Senior Living / Assisted Living
senior_living.rationale: Senior-living staffing (memory care, direct care, dining, maintenance) is year-round and census-driven rather than academic-calendar-driven like the generic acute-care hospital seasonality (HIMSS/Nursing Week/fall hiring ramp) it would otherwise inherit. Two real, non-clinical demand signals differentiate it: a Q4/Q1 flu-season staffing bump tied to resident-acuity/coverage-ratio requirements (CDC flu season runs Oct-Feb), and a January bump tied to new-fiscal-year budget approvals releasing headcount.
senior_living.source: Domain reasoning, not a fabricated statistic: senior-living census and staffing ratios are regulated and comparatively stable year-round (unlike acute-care hospital seasonality); flu season (CDC, Oct-Feb) increases resident acuity and required coverage ratios; most senior-living operators run a calendar fiscal year, so newly approved requisitions commonly release in January.

events: New fiscal-year budget approvals release headcount
1.recommendation: Increase spend -- newly approved requisitions and post-holiday attrition both open up in January.

2.recommendation: Maintain steady recruiting spend as flu-season coverage needs taper.

3.recommendation: Maintain steady, year-round recruiting spend proportional to census turnover.

5.recommendation: Maintain steady spend; use Nursing Week for employer-branding content.

7.recommendation: Maintain steady spend; summer brings modest frontline turnover.

9.recommendation: Begin ramping spend ahead of flu season's increased coverage-ratio requirements.

10.recommendation: Increase spend to meet flu-season coverage-ratio requirements.

11.recommendation: Maintain elevated spend for flu-season coverage and holiday PTO backfill.

events: Year-end planning for the January budget-cycle bump
12.recommendation: Maintain moderate spend for holiday coverage; prepare budget for the January budget-cycle bump.
